finding: coerceToDeclared runs the `isTemplateValue(raw)` early-return BEFORE the kind switch, so a json/textarea field whose text merely CONTAINS a reference is returned as a raw STRING instead of being JSON-parsed. Trigger: tool schema {"properties":{"filters":{"type":"object"}}} -> fieldKind='json' -> ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:177 is the only caller; the author types {"userId": "{{ inputs.user }}"}. TEMPLATE_RE matches, line 300 returns the raw string, so arguments.filters is persisted as the STRING '{"userId": "{{ inputs.user }}"}' rather than an object. The value silently changes type on the first keystroke, and the existing test only covers the whole-value case coerceToDeclared('{{ inputs.limit }}', ...). Partially-templated object/array arguments are the normal authoring pattern for a tool that takes structured input.

enumOptions (and choiceOptions, line 141) stringify every enum value with String(v) and ToolField.options carries no way back to the declared type, so a non-string enum is silently written to the workflow as a string. Trigger: {"properties":{"level":{"type":"integer","enum":[1,2,3]}}}. fieldKind checks `enum` FIRST (line 157) so kind='select', not 'integer'; ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:151 does onChange(v) with the option's string value and nothing coerces it -> arguments.level === "2" where the tool declares an integer. Identical for a boolean enum ([true,false] -> "true") and for multiselect (ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:162 value.map(String); coerceToDeclared's multiselect arm is never reached from that control).

Neither standard spelling of a NULLABLE property is understood, so both degrade to a raw JSON textarea. (a) `type` as an array: FieldSchema.type is typed `string` (workflowElicitSchema.ts:47) and the switch at 175 has no array branch, so {"q":{"type":["string","null"]}} falls to `default:` -> 'json'; the line-164 `field.type === 'array'` test likewise misses ["array","null"]. (b) anyOf-null: {"q":{"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"null"}]}} (what FastMCP/pydantic emit for Optional[str], i.e. the most common real MCP tool schema) fails the line-161 `choices.every(c => 'const' in c)` test, then hits switch(undefined) -> 'json'. The author gets a 4-row JSON box for a plain optional string, and typing 1234 into it yields the NUMBER 1234 via coerceToDeclared's JSON.parse where the schema requires a string.

`allOf` is not handled anywhere. Trigger: {"properties":{"level":{"allOf":[{"$ref":"#/$defs/Level"}],"default":"info"}}} — pydantic v1's spelling for an enum-typed field, and the standard way to attach a description to a $ref. There is no enum, no anyOf/oneOf and no `type` on the node, so fieldKind falls to `default:` -> 'json'. The referenced $defs entry (which DOES declare the enum) is never consulted because resolveSchema only follows a `$ref` that is a DIRECT key of the node, not one nested inside allOf. A closed value set renders as a free JSON box.

resolveSchema discards the referencing node's OWN sibling keywords: when `$ref` is present it returns resolveSchema(target,...) and never merges the node back. Trigger: {"properties":{"color":{"$ref":"#/$defs/Color","title":"Line colour","description":"Colour of the trend line","default":"red"}}} with $defs.Color = {"type":"string","enum":["red","blue"]}. describeToolSchema:236-243 then reads title/description/default off the RESOLVED def, so the field is labelled from the shared def (or falls back to the raw key `color`), shows no description, and loses `default: "red"` entirely. $ref-alongside-annotations is legal and common in JSON Schema 2020-12.

coerceToDeclared's `integer`, `number`, `switch` and `multiselect` arms are unreachable on the production path. The function has exactly ONE caller — ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:177 — inside the `case 'textarea': case 'json':` Textarea branch. Every other kind is edited by a typed control that calls onChange directly: InputNumber (line 140), Switch (128), Select (151), MultiSelect (163), and the default Input (190, which passes e.target.value uncoerced). So only kinds 'textarea' and 'json' ever reach the switch. The unit tests exercise the dead arms (toolSchemaForm.test.ts:156-158: coerceToDeclared('5', f('limit')) === 5, coerceToDeclared('true', f('verbose')) === true), which reads as coverage of a type-coercion step that never runs — and masks finding #2 above.

ToolFormSpec.overflowNames is computed but its VALUES are never read — only `.length` (ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:247). The overflow note says 'the rest can be set below', yet the free key/value section below only pre-creates rows for keys that ALREADY have a value (ToolStepForm.tsx:174/179 -> splitArguments -> `extra`, and splitArguments:281 builds `declared` from spec.fields, i.e. the KEPT 24 only). So for a tool declaring >24 properties the author is told N more arguments exist, is NOT told their names — which this spec is holding in overflowNames — and must type each key from memory. That is precisely the 'never make the author type what the system can enumerate' failure the module header (lines 6-11) says it exists to prevent.

SCHEMA_BUDGET.maxFields bounds the RENDERED fields but the cap is applied after the whole property set has been materialised, and the unbounded remainder is retained. describeToolSchema builds Object.keys(props), then two full `filter` passes, then `ordered.slice(24)` into overflowNames — which is kept alive on the spec for the lifetime of the memo despite never being read (see the api-friendliness row). A tool returning a 5,000-property input_schema allocates four full-length arrays per re-derivation. Bounded in practice by the HTTP response size, hence low, but the cap is in the wrong place: it should bound the enumeration, not just the render.

The textarea heuristic promotes a field to a multi-line control based on its DESCRIPTION length, not the value's: `(field.description?.length ?? 0) > 160`. Trigger: {"name":{"type":"string","maxLength":40,"description":"<180 chars of prose>"}} — a 40-char single-line name renders as a 3-row Textarea (ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:170-175) purely because the tool author wrote a thorough description. maxLength (40) explicitly says otherwise and is ignored in that branch.

lookupRef uses `name in bucket`, which walks the prototype chain, so a $defs pointer at an inherited key resolves to a prototype member. Trigger: {"$defs":{},"properties":{"x":{"$ref":"#/$defs/__proto__"}}} -> bucket['__proto__'] is Object.prototype, which isRecord() accepts, so it is returned as the field's FieldSchema and rendered (harmlessly, as 'json'). '#/$defs/constructor' and '#/$defs/toString' return functions and are rejected by isRecord, so nothing throws and there is no pollution — but the lookup should be Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(bucket, name) so an attacker-influenced pointer cannot silently resolve to something the tool never declared.

A root-level `$ref` is not resolved. describeToolSchema reads inputSchema['properties'] directly, so {"$ref":"#/$defs/Input","$defs":{"Input":{"type":"object","properties":{...},"required":[...]}}} yields props === undefined -> returns null -> the whole tool falls back to hand-typed key/value pairs. The schema is fully self-contained and this module's own resolveSchema could dereference it in one call; the fallback is taken for a schema it is capable of reading.

Adding a ToolFieldKind requires edits in three places and only two are type-checked. `fieldKind` (line 152) returns the kind and `ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:121` switches on it — but that switch ends in a `default:` (line 185) returning a plain Input, so a new union member compiles clean and silently renders as an untyped text box. coerceToDeclared (line 303) likewise has a `default:`. A `satisfies`-exhaustive mapping (or removing the two `default:` arms in favour of explicit cases) would make a new kind a compile error rather than a silent degradation.

resolveFindingStep takes loc.split('.')[0], but the location for WORKFLOW_BAD_STEP_ID (validate.rs:624) is the RAW step id — which by definition may be malformed. Trigger: a YAML-authored workflow with `- id: report.final` alongside `- id: report`, loaded into the builder (WorkflowBuilder.store.ts:159 load -> runValidate). The finding's location is 'report.final', head = 'report', so the copy "This step's internal name must start with a lowercase letter..." is attached to the WRONG step (or, with no 'report' step, to 'Whole workflow'). StepList.tsx:68 then flags the wrong row as invalid. The one finding whose job is to point at a bad id is the one that cannot.

The outputs guard is `loc.startsWith('outputs[')`, but WORKFLOW_DUPLICATE_OUTPUT_NAME (validate.rs:857) passes the BARE output name as its location (&o.name), not an outputs[...] path — only ref_check.rs:189 uses the bracketed form. So an output named the same as a step (the canonical pattern: outputs: [{name: summary, from: '{{ summary.output }}'}] next to `- id: summary`) would attribute a whole-workflow output finding to that step. LATENT ONLY: BuilderDef/toWorkflowDef (WorkflowBuilder.store.ts:25-63) never send `outputs`, so this code cannot fire from the builder today — it is guarded by an omission elsewhere, not by this function.

WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_SYNTAX interpolates the RAW backend message into author-facing copy, violating this file's own stated rules at lines 52-56 ('never name a YAML key, a Rust field, or a wire type') and the drift guard's stated purpose. The interpolated text is TemplateError's Display impl (template.rs:46-63), e.g. "unknown filter 'foo' (supported: json, raw)" or "cannot access field 'x' on a non-object value (path 'a.b')", so the person reads: "A reference in this step isn't written correctly (cannot access field 'x' on a non-object value (path 'a.b'))." The backend test only checks that the CODE key exists in this file, so it cannot catch a humanisation that re-emits the wire message verbatim.

WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE (line 93) and WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE (line 95) carry BYTE-IDENTICAL copy, erasing the distinction the two codes exist to make. Backend: UNSAFE (validate.rs:1045) fires on a literal '..' or leading '/' in prompt_file — the author typed a bad path; ESCAPE (validate.rs:1059) fires when a syntactically fine relative path CANONICALIZES outside the bundle — a symlink out of the bundle. The fix differs (edit the path vs. remove the symlink) but the sentence is the same.

WORKFLOW_STEP_DESCRIPTION_TOO_LONG says 'shorten it to under 200 characters', but validate.rs:645 rejects only `desc.chars().count() > MAX_STEP_DESCRIPTION_CHARS` (=200, validate.rs:272) — exactly 200 characters is VALID. The instruction is off by one and tells the author to delete a character that is allowed.

WORKFLOW_BAD_STEP_ID ("This step's internal name must start with a lowercase letter...") and WORKFLOW_DUPLICATE_STEP_ID ("rename one of them", line 75) instruct the author to edit a step id, but the builder exposes no step-id control anywhere: StepConfigPanel.tsx renders description/depends_on plus the per-kind form, stepForms.ts mints ids in createStep (line 95-96), and no component patches `id`. Both findings are only reachable for a YAML-imported workflow and are unfixable from the surface that displays them — the copy asks for an action the UI does not offer.

Four backend limits are hardcoded into English sentences here with no drift guard: '50 is the limit' (line 62 vs validate.rs:610), 'under 200 characters' (78 vs MAX_STEP_DESCRIPTION_CHARS=200, validate.rs:272), 'the longest allowed wait is 30 minutes' (107 vs ELICIT_TIMEOUT_HARD_CAP_MS=1_800_000, validate.rs:279), 'the maximum is 20' (109 vs MAX_PARALLEL_HARD_CAP=20, validate.rs:270). All four are CORRECT today (verified), but validation_codes_are_registered_and_humanised (validate.rs:2004) only asserts the quoted CODE literal is present in this file — it never compares the numbers. Bumping any cap silently makes the author-facing copy lie, in the one file whose whole purpose is a checked humanisation contract.

severityOf defaults an ABSENT severity to 'error', while the generated contract declares it optional (api-client/types.ts:7440 `severity?: Severity`). StepList.tsx:39-41 concatenates attributeFindings(validation.errors) with attributeFindings(validation.warnings) and then relies solely on this field for the per-step badge counts, discarding the authoritative signal (which array the finding arrived in). If the backend ever adds skip_serializing_if to ValidationError.severity — legal under the generated type — every warning would be counted and badged as a blocking error. Passing the known severity into attributeFindings would make the wrong state unrepresentable.

Two exports have no production consumer. HUMANISED_CODES (line 161) is imported only by validationCopy.test.ts:7 — the Rust drift guard (validate.rs:2046) greps this file's raw TEXT for `"CODE"` literals and never touches this export, so its stated role ('drift-guard surface') is not what the guard actually uses. WORKFLOW_LEVEL (line 234) is written by indexFindingsByStep (241) but that bucket is never read: StepList.tsx:68 only does findingsByStep.get(step.id), and BuilderValidationPanel.tsx:81-82 re-derives from attributeFindings + findingStepTitle. The workflow-level counts are computed on every render and discarded.

A server-side 403 is misclassified as 'unreachable'. mcp/handlers/runtime.rs:79-87 returns 403 USER_NO_ACCESS 'You do not have access to this server' when the caller HOLDS mcp_servers::read but lacks per-server access — a condition hasPermissionNow(Permissions.McpServersRead) at line 61 structurally cannot detect. The catch at 85 labels every throw 'unreachable', so failureMessage:167 renders the self-contradicting sentence: `Couldn't reach "web_search" (You do not have access to this server) — enter the tool name and arguments by hand.` The 'no-permission' variant exists for exactly this case and is only ever reached via the client-side global-permission pre-check. Branching on `(error as {status?: number}).status === 403` (the api-client stamps it, core.ts:729) would classify it correctly.

failureMessage's 'unreachable' arm interpolates a raw api-client Error.message into an author-facing sentence. sdk/packages/framework/src/api-client/core.ts:678 defaults errorMessage to `HTTP error! status: ${response.status}` and line 712 to `HTTP error! status: 502 - ${textResponse}` when the body is not JSON. So a proxy returning an HTML error page produces: `Couldn't reach "web_search" (HTTP error! status: 502 - <!DOCTYPE html><html>...) — enter the tool name and arguments by hand.` — a machine code plus an unbounded third-party document pasted into an Alert description (ToolStepForm.tsx:244). The store's own doc (line 22-23) says every failure maps to VISIBLE author-facing copy; this one maps to a transport dump.

The store's stated contract — 'refetching once per builder mount is CORRECT' (lines 12-15) — does not hold. Its only consumer is ToolStepForm, which StepConfigPanel.tsx:88 mounts as `<StepForm key={step.id} ...>`; defineLocalStore.use (store-kit.ts:632-645) creates the zustand api inside a useRef that is re-initialised on every remount. So a FRESH catalog instance is created on every step selection, not once per builder. Repro: a workflow with two tool steps on the same server — clicking step A, step B, step A issues three GET /api/mcp/servers/{id}/tools calls, each of which may spawn/handshake a stdio MCP server. Both byServerId and the `inflight` Set (line 52) are per-instance, so neither the cache nor the coalescing guard can dedupe across selections, and the byServerId map (documented at 41-43 as letting 'two names for one server share a fetch') can only ever hold one entry.

Three declared members are never used anywhere in either UI workspace (verified by repo-wide grep for markUnknown / unknownNames / .invalidate on this store). `markUnknown` (111) has no caller and `unknownNames` (47) is read by nothing — the 'unknown-server' failure it was meant to feed is produced independently by entryForServerName:148-153. `invalidate` (118) also has no caller, and its doc comment cites a "try again" affordance that does not exist: ToolStepForm renders the failure as a static Alert (line 239-246) with no retry control. Roughly a fifth of the store's surface is unreachable, and the invalidate doc documents behaviour the UI does not offer.

invalidate() deletes the cache entry but does NOT clear `inflight`, so calling it during a fetch leaves that serverId registered: the next load() short-circuits at line 56 and returns with no fetch, and the still-running pre-invalidation request then writes its (by definition stale) result into byServerId at 78-101. The repo's own core/coalescedLoader.ts documents this exact bug and solves it with a generation counter ('Clearing only the cache would hand the next reader the still-registered pre-invalidation promise', lines 16-20). Currently LATENT because invalidate has no callers — it becomes live the moment the documented 'try again' button is added.

The store hand-rolls cache + in-flight coalescing that src-app/ui/src/core/coalescedLoader.ts already provides — a module explicitly extracted for reuse ('Reusable by any other "several stores want the same list on boot" case', lines 6-9) — and re-implements it with strictly weaker semantics: no TTL, no generation guard on a superseded request (see the invalidate row), and a second caller gets `undefined` back rather than the shared promise (line 56 returns nothing, so `await catalog.load(...)` resolves before the data exists). Either adopt the loader per serverId or state in the header why per-server keying rules it out.

load(serverId, serverName) takes the name purely to embed it in a failure message, and nothing links the two arguments. The caller must independently keep them consistent — ToolStepForm.tsx:137 passes `serverId` (derived by entryForServerName from step.server) and `step.server` separately; entryForServerName already resolved BOTH from the same match object and could return the pair. A caller that passes a stale name after the author renames a server produces a failure Alert naming the wrong server, with no compile-time or runtime check.

Apostrophe style is inconsistent inside this one change. failureMessage uses ASCII apostrophes throughout — "You don't have permission to list this server's tools" (165), "Couldn't reach" (167), "which isn't one of the servers available to you" (163) — while the sibling component added in the same diff writes the same possessive typographically: ToolStepForm.tsx:275 'Loading this server\u2019s tools\u2026'. The two sentences appear in the same control within seconds of each other. ASCII is the dominant style in the workflow module (only 4 U+2019 occurrences module-wide), so ToolStepForm is the outlier — but the pair should be settled one way before this ships.

REJECTED — falsy defaults. Checked default:false / default:0 / default:"" end to end. ToolField.default is `unknown` and assigned unguarded (`default: schema.default`, line 242), the consumer gates on `field.default !== undefined` (ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:73), and valueToText(false)==='false' / valueToText(0)==='0' (line 327-331 falls to JSON.stringify for non-strings). Falsy defaults survive intact. Only default:"" renders the empty sentence 'Defaults to .', which is cosmetic and lives in the consumer, not here.

REJECTED — self-referential $ref infinite recursion. Verified terminating: with $defs.Node = {"$ref":"#/$defs/Node"} the first hop pushes the ref onto `stack`, the second hits `stack.includes(ref)` (line 129) and returns null; a long non-cyclic chain is cut by stack.length >= maxRefDepth. Mutual recursion (A->B->A) is cut identically. resolveSchema also never recurses into nested `properties`, so there is no second unbounded axis. The explicit-stack claim in the header holds.

REJECTED — hostile/malformed input throwing. Constructed and traced: inputSchema as null/string/array/number; properties as a string or array; required containing non-strings ([1,null]); enum as a non-array; anyOf/oneOf as a string; items as a tuple ARRAY (`"items":[{...}]`); items.enum a non-array; enumNames shorter than enum or a string; maxLength a string. Every one is guarded by isRecord / Array.isArray / optional chaining, and none throws or returns a shape ToolArgumentsForm crashes on — the documented 'degrade to the escape hatch, never throw' contract (lines 199-205) holds.

REJECTED — TEMPLATE_RE regex statefulness. The literal has no `g`/`y` flag, so RegExp.prototype.test carries no lastIndex across calls; isTemplateValue is deterministic per input despite the shared module-level regex. Also checked the lazy `[\s\S]*?` against a value containing many `{{`: no catastrophic backtracking (no nested quantifier).

REJECTED — 'a failed fetch is cached forever'. The cache-hit guard requires `existing.failure == null` (line 59), so a failed OR no-permission entry always falls through and re-fetches on the next load(). Also checked for a permanently-loading entry: inflight is cleared in `finally` (102-104) and both the success and catch paths set loading:false, so no path leaves loading:true. What actually re-triggers the retry is a remount or a serverId change (ToolStepForm.tsx:136-139 deps), which per the confirmed lifecycle row happens on every step switch — so retries are frequent, not absent.

REJECTED — set() after unmount writing to a dead consumer. defineLocalStore (store-kit.ts:632-658) holds the zustand api in a useRef and its unmount cleanup only runs __destroy__, which detaches EventBus listeners; it does not tear down the store api. A late set() therefore writes to a store with no remaining subscribers — no React state-update-on-unmounted warning, no leak beyond the instance itself being GC'd with the component.

REJECTED — cache-hit check running BEFORE the permission check (57-59 vs 61). Order does matter in principle: an entry fetched while permitted is still served after a mid-session permission loss. But the entry was legitimately fetched, contains only tool names/descriptions the user was already shown, and the whole store instance is destroyed on the next step switch. No leak of anything not already disclosed; not worth a change.

REJECTED — attributeFindings scanning `steps` twice per finding (steps.find inside resolveFindingStep at 192, then steps.findIndex at 211). O(findings x steps), and the backend caps a workflow at 50 steps (validate.rs:610), so the worst case is a few thousand string comparisons per validation round, re-run on a 400ms debounce. Measurably free; a Map<id,index> would be premature.

REJECTED — response-shape mismatch. Checked against the generated contract: ListToolsResponse.tools is NON-optional (api-client/types.ts:3082-3084), so `res.tools ?? []` (line 80) is redundant but harmless, not a nullable-treated-as-non-null bug. Tool.input_schema is `unknown` (types.ts:6542-6546) and describeToolSchema's parameter is `unknown` — an exact match, and every narrowing is done defensively inside. Tool.description is optional and is handled with a ternary at ToolStepForm.tsx:145. No contract violation found in these three files.

REJECTED — vocabulary duplication in toolSchemaForm. It imports FieldSchema/TitledChoice from ../workflowElicitSchema rather than declaring a second JSON-Schema type set, imports nothing outside the workflow module, and has no React/store dependency (it is pure and directly unit-tested). The one real consequence of that reuse is that FieldSchema.type is `string` and so cannot express a type ARRAY — logged separately under correctness-logic, not as a coupling defect.

REJECTED — mixed voice in HUMAN_COPY. Entries alternate between declarative ('This step needs a prompt.') and imperative ('Choose the server this step should call.'), but the split tracks a real distinction — describing a broken state vs. naming the single action that fixes it — and every entry stays one sentence with a consistent em-dash-before-the-remedy pattern. Style preference, not a defect. Also checked every entry for a leaked machine code or YAML/Rust key: none found except WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_SYNTAX, logged separately.

REJECTED — HUMAN_COPY as a closed map every new code must edit. Verified this is the intended, well-supported design, not drift-prone: adding a code is a ONE-place edit here, an unmapped code degrades to the backend message (humaniseFinding:172-174) rather than to nothing, and validate.rs:2004 fails the backend suite in BOTH directions (emitted-but-unregistered, and registered-but-unhumanised). Cross-checked all 41 registered VALIDATION_CODES against HUMAN_COPY's 41 keys and the /validate-def handler (handlers/dev.rs:938-963, which only calls validate_collecting, i.e. validate.rs + ref_check.rs): every code this surface can emit is mapped. No gap.

REJECTED — SCHEMA_BUDGET / ToolFormSpec / ToolField as unused exports. SCHEMA_BUDGET is exported for toolSchemaForm.test.ts:129-135 (which derives the overflow case from it rather than hardcoding 24) — a legitimate test seam, and it is read on the production path at lines 226-227 and 129. ToolField/ToolFormSpec are imported by ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:16-17. isTemplateValue, splitArguments, valueToText and describeToolSchema all have production callers (ToolArgumentsForm.tsx, ToolStepForm.tsx:15/152/174). Only the coerceToDeclared arms and overflowNames' contents are genuinely unreached, logged separately.
